title: Chapter 208: This Is a Love Song
html:
The woman’s face was startlingly white, her features contorting with agitation. She wound one slender arm around Gu Feiyu’s neck and traced an icy finger down his cheek.

She licked away her bright lipstick and pressed her thin, purplish lips near Gu Feiyu’s ear. “When two people love the same thing, the fairest solution is to cut it in half and share.”

The cleaver sliced through a button on his uniform, though her movements remained soft and gentle. The guard struggled to open his eyes; he had not entirely lost consciousness.

“My sister and I both received our love. He was the first for each of us.” She rested against Gu Feiyu’s chest. “Your personality resembles his. I planned to wait a few months before inviting you upstairs, but those people have found me. I must leave the city soon.”

Listening to his heartbeat, she raised her head. “Don’t worry. I won’t hurt you.”

She entered the bedroom, pulled the black suitcase from atop the wardrobe, and removed an ancient tape recorder. Kneeling beside it, she selected a dust-covered cassette and slowly kissed its edge as though performing a ritual.

She inserted the cassette and pressed play. A young man’s voice drifted from the recorder, clear, warm, and full of love. Cleaver in hand, the woman listened silently to the love song.

“I’ve made about ten copies of this tape, but most of them have been lost.”

The familiar melody filled the living room and carried her years into the past. She tossed aside Gu Feiyu’s uniform, retrieved a coil of rope from beneath the sofa, tied him securely, and dragged him into the bathroom.

From the wardrobe, Chen Ge witnessed everything. “The locked freezer, the oversized bathtub… She prepared all of this. She’s completely insane.”

If he did not act, Gu Feiyu would die. Chen Ge silenced his phone, positioned himself beside the bedroom door, lifted the vanity chair, and called the guard’s number.

The woman lowered Gu Feiyu into the bathtub just as his phone rang in the living room. “Why now?”

Barefoot, she returned to the living room and picked up the uniform from the corner. As she searched its pockets, Chen Ge crept up behind her.

Sensing him, she began to turn—but before she could face him, Chen Ge swung the heavy chair.

She had never expected another person in the apartment. The blow dropped her to the floor, blood streaming from her scalp. Her eyes bulged as she glared at Chen Ge.

“Why are you here?!”

Chen Ge did not waste words, especially while his opponent could still move. He brought the chair down on the same spot again. Her head lolled sideways. Already frail, she could no longer stand.

Chen Ge freed Gu Feiyu and used the rope to bind the woman’s arms and legs. “Who would have thought the two missions overlapped? This does make things easier.”

He replaced the cassette with his own. The singing died, leaving only white noise.

“Those who disrespect life will be disrespected by life.”

Fresh blood stained the woman’s face. From the floor, she continued staring at Chen Ge—not with fear, but with bewildered shock. He called Inspector Lee. The moment the call connected, every light in the apartment went out.

She escaped from the Third Sick Hall, so she must carry an entity from behind the door.

Chen Ge switched on his phone’s flashlight and drew the cleaver from his backpack.

The red cloth fluttered to the floor as Chen Ge surveyed the darkness. Then fingernails began scraping across the front door, the shrill sound setting his nerves on edge.

It’s that white shadow!

The first scratch told Chen Ge what had arrived.

“Is anyone home?” An indistinct, unnatural voice sounded beyond the door and repeated the question. Cleaver raised, Chen Ge did not know whether answering would help or doom him.

When it repeated itself the seventh time, the voice said, “Is anyone home? If no one’s home, I’m coming in.”

The front door creaked open. A human-sized white figure stood beyond it—the fourth such monster Chen Ge had encountered, after the mirror monster, the thin monster, and the broken-arm monster. Its face was blurred and incomplete, but it moved with terrifying speed.

Chen Ge held the cleaver before his chest. The creature radiated menace. It was weaker than the thin monster but far stronger than an ordinary mirror monster. At the Third Sick Hall, the thin monster had hunted him relentlessly; without Zhang Ya, he might not have survived.

The white figure faced him, then blurred to his side in an instant. Chen Ge swung. As the cleaver cut through it, the creature shrieked in pain and glared at him.

Its white face shifted before his eyes until it resembled Patient No. 2. Yet the features would not hold, as though repeated surgeries had left the entire face so fragile that any expression might dislodge it.

As the face drew near, Chen Ge stabbed at the ghost with the ballpoint pen from his pocket. Both struggled fiercely, neither noticing the anguished male cry beginning to echo through the room.

“So painful…”

The pen lodged in the white figure’s forehead. It seized Chen Ge’s wrist and slowly pressed its face toward his, as though trying to steal it.

“So painful, so painful, so painful!”

Just before it touched the tip of Chen Ge’s nose, an unseen force wrenched it backward, pulling its hair taut.

“So painful!” The cry came from behind the figure. Both Chen Ge and the bound woman reacted.

“Xu Yin! Is that you?” The woman reacted even more strongly than Chen Ge. Bound hand and foot, she pushed against the floor with her forehead, struggling upright.

The woman’s distraction caused the white figure’s face to dissolve and its presence to weaken.

“What’s happening? Was she controlling the white figure?” Alone in retaining his composure, Chen Ge watched the creature weaken and seized the chance to strike.

The Tape Ghost had immobilized it, presenting the perfect opening. Yet at the last instant, Xu Yin released his grip. He seemed to recognize the woman on the floor.

“So painful…”
